title: News Failure
teaches: The News Failure as we trade it: big, dated news meets the opposite reaction, a bad-news gap down on heavy volume that is back over the prior close by the close, above the 200-day; the buy is a market order as price trades back over the prior close, the stop sits a few cents under the news day's low (wide, so the size comes from the stop), a third comes off at 3R and 5R with the rest on the trail, and a loss at the stop is the system working. The short is the mirror.

questions.q: In a News Failure long, what does the stock do on the news day?
choices: Gaps down on bad news, yet closes green
Gaps up on good news and holds the gap
Gaps down on bad news and keeps falling
Drifts sideways on no news or gap
questions.answer: Gaps down on bad news, yet closes green
questions.why: Gaps down on bad news, yet closes green, back over the prior close. The card puts it plainly: the long is the gap down that closes back above the prior close the same day. Our scan uses a stand-in for the news. It is an open 4% or more under the prior close, on 2 times or more the prior 50-day volume. It does not mean any bounce. A gap that closes low and stays down means the news worked.
questions.lesson_line: Bad news, a gap down, and a close back over the prior close.

wrong.Gaps up on good news and holds the gap: That is the News Gapper, good news that holds.
wrong.Gaps down on bad news and keeps falling: News that keeps the stock down worked. It is the bear gap, not a failure.
wrong.Drifts sideways on no news or gap: A News Failure needs a dated catalyst behind a real gap.

questions.simple: It gaps down on bad news, then closes back over the prior close, so the bad news failed to hold it down.

reasons: rests on the criteria card's proposed criterion (owner default, not yet ruled) (nf.scan_standin, the look-alike lines)

questions.q: Shapiro's test: the news is bullish, but by the end of the day the market closes down.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. That is Shapiro's news failure. Bullish news comes out, yet by the end of the day the market fails and closes down. No other bearish news explains it. His own example adds crowded longs and a red close for the day. These are his words, not our full rule. Our long is the mirror: a bad-news gap down that closes back above the prior close.
questions.lesson_line: News points one way and the close goes the other.
questions.simple: True. Shapiro calls it a news failure when the news is good but the market still closes down that day.

reasons: same-day close test is a held decision (D-087)

questions.q: Tap the word that fits the blank.
questions.sentence: A News Failure long is bought as price trades back over the ___ close.
questions.answer: prior
questions.why: Prior. The long is a market order when price trades back over the prior close on the news day, red to green. Entries are market orders. The card also allows buying at the close if you wait for Shapiro's confirmation. The trigger is not a weekly or monthly close, or a moving average.
questions.lesson_line: Buy as price trades back over the prior close.
questions.simple: Prior. You buy as the price climbs back over yesterday's close, the moment the day turns from red to green.

reasons: the red-to-green entry is a proposed card line tied to D-087

At 3% under your buy, whatever the chart
questions.answer: A few cents under the news day's low
questions.why: A few cents under the news day's low so far, not exactly on it. For a short it mirrors: a few cents over the news day's high. The prior close is the trigger, not the stop. If price takes out the news day's extreme, the turn was not picked. The stop is a chart level, not a fixed percent.
questions.lesson_line: Long: under the news day's low. Short: over its high.

wrong.A few cents over the news day's high: That is the short's stop, mirrored.
wrong.At 3% under your buy, whatever the chart: The stop is the news day's extreme, not a fixed percent.
wrong.Just under the prior day's close: The news day's low is the extreme. The prior close is the trigger, not the stop.

questions.simple: A few cents under the news day's low, because a new low means the turn you bought did not happen.

reasons: rests on the owner's rulebook (F62)

questions.q: A News Failure long must be above the 200-day, unless it is a parabolic long.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. No longs below the 200-day simple moving average, unless it is a parabolic long. The News Failure long follows that hard rule. The rulebook's mirror for shorts: only below the 200-day, unless parabolic.
questions.lesson_line: Longs live above the 200-day. The News Failure is no exception.
questions.simple: True. We take no longs below the 200-day average unless the move is parabolic, and this setup follows that rule.

reasons: rests on the owner's rulebook (B26)

questions.q: With no news feed, a gap of 4% or more on 2 times the prior 50-day volume stands in for the news.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. That is the card's stand-in, since there is no news feed. The stock opens 4% or more under the prior close, on 2 times or more the prior 50-day volume. For the short it is 4% or more over.
questions.lesson_line: No news feed, so a big gap on double volume stands in for it.
questions.simple: True. With no news feed, a gap of 4% or more on at least twice the 50-day volume stands in for the news.

reasons: the gap-and-volume stand-in is a proposed card line, not an owner ruling

questions.q: Good news gaps a stock up, but it closes under the prior close. What is that?
choices: A News Gapper, but a weak one
An Oops Reversal, but with news
A News Failure, the mirror
A bear gap, the start of a fall
questions.answer: A News Failure, the mirror
questions.why: A News Failure, the mirror. Good news gaps the stock up and it closes red, under the prior close. A News Gapper gaps on the same good news but closes green and holds the gap. An Oops needs an open under the prior low and has no news requirement. A bear gap starts with bad news that keeps the stock down.
questions.lesson_line: Same headline, opposite close: gapper holds, failure fades.

wrong.A News Gapper, but a weak one: A News Gapper closes green and holds the gap. This one closed under the prior close.
wrong.An Oops Reversal, but with news: An Oops opens under the prior low, and this one gapped up. Read the close against the news instead.
wrong.A bear gap, the start of a fall: A bear gap starts with bad news that gaps the stock down and keeps it down. This gap was up, on good news.

questions.simple: It is the short side of a News Failure, because good news gapped it up and it still closed under yesterday's close.

reasons: the same-day close test is a held decision (D-087)

questions.q: Bad news gaps a stock down and it closes at the low, staying down. What is it?
choices: A News Failure long on the open
A News Gapper that held its gap
A Red to Green on the second day
A bear gap or earnings breakdown
questions.answer: A bear gap or earnings breakdown
questions.why: A bear gap or an earnings breakdown. Bad news gapped it down, and it closed low and stayed down, so the news worked. Calling that a News Failure is a listed mistake. The failure needs the opposite close: back above the prior close the same day.
questions.lesson_line: If the gap down keeps going, the news worked. That is not a failure.

wrong.A News Failure long on the open: The long closes back over the prior close. This stock did not.
wrong.A News Gapper that held its gap: A News Gapper gaps on good news and holds it.
wrong.A Red to Green on the second day: Red to Green reclaims the prior close. This did not.

questions.simple: It is a bear gap or an earnings breakdown, because the stock stayed down, so the bad news did its job.

reasons: rests on the criteria card's look-alike lines and listed mistake (house source)

questions.q: How is the News Failure short entered?
choices: Market, over the prior day's high
Market, back under the prior close
A limit order at the day's high
Market, at the open into the gap up
questions.answer: Market, back under the prior close
questions.why: Market, back under the prior close. The short is a market order when price trades back under the prior close, green to red, or at the close. Entries are market orders, not limit orders. The prior high is not the trigger. Shorting the open bets against the news before it has failed.
questions.lesson_line: The short mirrors the long: under the prior close.

wrong.Market, over the prior day's high: The trigger is the prior close, not the prior high. The short waits for price to trade back under that close.
wrong.A limit order at the day's high: Entries are market orders when the trigger trades.
wrong.Market, at the open into the gap up: That shorts the good news before it fails. The trigger is price trading back under the prior close.

questions.simple: At market as the price falls back under yesterday's close, because that is the moment the good news fails.

deeper.trap: Shorting the open into good news bets against it before it has failed. The market has shown nothing yet. The setup waits for the failure itself: price trading back under the prior close, green to red. Until then there is no trade.

reasons: the short entry is a proposed card line; traded shorts wait on D-001

questions.q: Five or more stocks with the same News Failure shape on one day point to news about the market.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. The card's line is fewer than 5 such events on the same day. A same-day cluster, many names showing one shape on one day, means the news was the market, not the stock. So a crowd of the same shape is a market read, not a stock setup.
questions.lesson_line: A crowd of the same shape on one day means a market story, not a stock story.
questions.simple: True, because when 5 or more stocks show one shape on one day, the cause is the market, not one stock.

reasons: rests on the criteria card's proposed criterion (owner default, not yet ruled) (nf.not_market_wide)

questions.q: What minimum price and daily trading does a News Failure need?
choices: $5 and $5 million a day
$20 and $100 million a day
$10 and $20 million a day
$10 and 1 million shares a day
questions.answer: $10 and $20 million a day
questions.why: $10 and $20 million a day. We trade only stocks at $10 or more that trade at least $20 million a day. The News Failure card uses the same floor. These are minimums, and the second is in dollars traded, not in shares.
questions.lesson_line: Price $10 or more and $20 million or more traded a day.

wrong.$5 and $5 million a day: Too thin. The floor is $10 and $20 million a day.
wrong.$20 and $100 million a day: That is stricter than the minimum. The floor is $10 and $20 million a day.
wrong.$10 and 1 million shares a day: The floor is in dollars traded, $20 million a day, not a share count.

questions.simple: At least $10 a share and $20 million traded a day, the same floor we use for every stock.

reasons: rests on the owner's rulebook (B23)

questions.q: Tap the word that fits the blank.
questions.sentence: No new buy or short in the ___ sessions before a scheduled report.
questions.why: 3. No new buy or short in the 3 sessions before a scheduled report. Our rulebook says the same for buys: no new buys in the 3 days before an earnings report. A trade already on is held through a report only if it is up 5R.
questions.lesson_line: Three sessions before a report, no new trade.
questions.simple: 3. We open no new trade in the 3 sessions before a scheduled report.

reasons: rests on the owner's rulebook (B22)

questions.q: Which close grades the long up?
choices: The bottom 25% of the day's range
Right on the prior close, unchanged
Top 25%, after undercutting the low
Anywhere green, even by a few cents
questions.answer: Top 25%, after undercutting the low
questions.why: The top 25% of the range, after the low undercut the prior day's low, an Oops shape. That raises the long's grade. The A+ cue goes further: the gap erased and the close near the far end of the range. A close just back above the prior close still counts as a failure. It does not earn this grade-up.
questions.lesson_line: A strong close in the top quarter grades the long up.

wrong.The bottom 25% of the day's range: That is the short's shape, not the long's.
wrong.Anywhere green, even by a few cents: A small green close can still count, but it does not grade up. That takes the top 25% after an undercut.
wrong.Right on the prior close, unchanged: The long needs a close back above the prior close. A close right on it is not even a failure.

questions.simple: A close in the top quarter of the day's range, after dipping under the prior day's low, grades the long up.

reasons: rests on the criteria card's proposed criterion (owner default, not yet ruled) (nf.grade_shape)

questions.q: Shapiro says positioning alone is enough to take the trade.
questions.answer: False
questions.why: False. In Shapiro's words, trader positioning is not enough to execute the trade; you also need market confirmation. His example is bullish news while the market closes red for the day. That is a news failure. These are his words, quoted as his view, not a UCT rule.
questions.lesson_line: Crowding is half of it. The failed news is the other half.
questions.simple: False, because Shapiro says positioning alone is not enough and the market must also confirm it.

questions.q: The stock is already well past the prior close when you look. What is the limit?
choices: Skip if more than 10% past the close
Skip if over 4% past the trigger
Buy any time that day, with a stop
Skip if over 4% past the day's low
questions.answer: Skip if over 4% past the trigger
questions.why: Skip if over 4% past the trigger. If the stock already moved more than 4% past the trigger, skip it. For a long the trigger is the prior close, not the day's low. Chasing costs size, not risk: the stop stays put, so the distance grows and the shares shrink. Shapiro's line fits: I miss a trade, I miss it.
questions.lesson_line: Past 4% beyond the trigger, skip it. Shapiro: I miss a trade, I miss it.

wrong.Skip if more than 10% past the close: The limit is 4% past the trigger.
wrong.Skip if over 4% past the day's low: The 4% is measured from the trigger, the prior close for a long, not from the day's low.

questions.simple: Skip it if the price is over 4% past the trigger, because a chase stretches the stop distance and shrinks the size.

reasons: rests on the owner's rulebook (C28)

questions.q: Bought at 86.36 with the stop at 81.48. How far under the buy is the stop, in percent?
questions.why: 5.7%. The distance from 86.36 down to 81.48 is 5.7% of the buy. Our stop usually sits within about 3% of the buy, so this one is wide. The size comes from the stop, so a wider stop means a smaller size. If the honest stop does not fit the risk, skip the trade. AAOI's stop was exactly this wide.
questions.lesson_line: Wide stop, small size. Measure the stop in percent first.
questions.simple: 5.7%. That stop is wider than our usual 3%, so the size must shrink to keep the same risk.

deeper.trap: A wide stop tempts you to pull it closer so the size looks normal again. The card names that mistake: tightening the stop to make the size work. Skip instead. The stop stays a few cents under the news day's low, and the size follows it.

reasons: computed key
rests on the owner's rulebook (A3, A13)

questions.q: Bought at 40.00 with the stop at 38.00. Where is 3R?
questions.why: 46.00. One R is the buy minus the stop: 40.00 minus 38.00. Add three of those to the buy. The hard rule takes the first third off at 3R.
questions.lesson_line: Know your 3R before you buy. The first third comes off there.
questions.simple: $46.00. One R is the distance from the buy to the stop, and 3R adds three of those on top of the buy.

deeper.example: SEDG on 2025-11-05 was bought at 31.83 with the stop at 30.23, a 5.0% stop. It reached 3R the next day, and its best move reached 10.5R.

reasons: computed key
rests on the owner's rulebook (B19)

questions.q: Shapiro's stop is hit only by a close beyond the extreme. What is ours?
choices: The same, a close beyond the extreme
A mental stop, watched all day
A real stop order, hit intraday
No stop; a small size caps the risk
questions.answer: A real stop order, hit intraday
questions.why: A real stop order with the broker, hit intraday. Every position has one, not a stop kept in your head. Shapiro's version is hit only when a session closes beyond the failure day's extreme. The card says it tested no better and it is not ours.
questions.lesson_line: Real stop order, not a mental stop and not a close-only stop.

wrong.The same, a close beyond the extreme: Ours is a real stop order with the broker. It is hit intraday.
wrong.A mental stop, watched all day: A stop kept in your head is not allowed.
wrong.No stop; a small size caps the risk: Every position has a real stop order with the broker. A small size does not replace it.

questions.simple: A real stop order sits with the broker and can fill during the day, not only on a close.

reasons: rests on the owner's rulebook (D41)

questions.q: Once the News Failure trade is on, the stop can be moved wider if it keeps getting close.
questions.answer: False
questions.why: False. The stop is the exit, and it only moves in the trade's favor, never down or wider. The one exception is the gap rule, when price gaps through the stop.
questions.lesson_line: The stop moves only in your favor.
questions.simple: False. Once the trade is on, the stop only moves in your favor and never wider.

deeper.trap: Widening a stop that keeps getting close turns a planned loss into a bigger one. The only time a stop moves wider is a gap through it, and even then a loss past 2R means out.

reasons: rests on the owner's rulebook (A4)

questions.q: How is the last third of a News Failure trailed?
choices: A close beyond the 10-day or 21-day
A close beyond the 200-day average
A fixed 5% under the move's high
An intraday touch of the 10-day average
questions.answer: A close beyond the 10-day or 21-day
questions.why: A close beyond the 10-day or 21-day. Trail the last third with a close beyond the 10-day for a fast mover, or the 21-day for a steadier one. For a long, sell on a close below it. It takes a close, not an intraday touch. Not the 200-day, and not a fixed percent.
questions.lesson_line: The last third rides the trail and leaves on a close beyond it.

wrong.A close beyond the 200-day average: The trail is the 10-day for fast movers or the 21-day for steadier ones.
wrong.A fixed 5% under the move's high: A fixed percent ignores the chart. The trail is the average.
wrong.An intraday touch of the 10-day average: The trail sells on a close beyond the average, not on an intraday touch.

questions.simple: It rides until a daily close beyond the 10-day average for a fast mover, or the 21-day for a steadier one.

reasons: rests on the owner's rulebook (E52)

questions.q: A trade gaps through the stop. What decides the new stop?
choices: The prior day's close or the open
The extreme of the first 30 minutes
The 10-day average at the open
The extreme of the first 5-minute bar
questions.answer: The extreme of the first 30 minutes
questions.why: The extreme of the first 30 minutes. For a long, the low of the first 30-minute bar of the gap-down day is the new stop. For a short, it is the high. If that takes the loss past 2R, get out. This gap rule is the one exception to the stop never moving wider.
questions.lesson_line: Gap through the stop: the first 30 minutes decide.

wrong.The prior day's close or the open: The extreme of the first 30 minutes sets the new stop.
wrong.The 10-day average at the open: The 10-day is the trail, not the gap stop.
wrong.The extreme of the first 5-minute bar: The rule uses the first 30 minutes, not the first 5.

questions.simple: The first 30 minutes of the gap day set the new stop, and if that loss is past 2R you get out.

reasons: rests on the owner's rulebook (B20)

questions.q: A News Failure still under 1R after 10 sessions is held until the stop or the trail decides.
questions.answer: False
questions.why: False. A trade still under 1R after 10 trading days is sold, freeing the money. This time stop does not wait for the stop or the trail. It applies to the News Failure like any other trade.
questions.lesson_line: Ten sessions under 1R, and the money moves on.
questions.simple: False. If it is still under 1R after 10 sessions, you sell it and free the money.

reasons: rests on the owner's rulebook (C33)

questions.q: Does the day pass the gap-and-volume test for news?
choices: No; the gap down is under 4%
No; volume must be 5x the average
Yes; the gap and volume both clear
Yes; the 2.4x volume alone is enough
questions.answer: Yes; the gap and volume both clear
questions.why: Yes. The open of 47.80 is more than 4% under the 50.00 close. Volume is 2.4 times the 50-day average, over the 2 times the test asks. Both parts must clear. Passing only flags the day; the reversal back over the prior close is still needed.
questions.lesson_line: A gap of 4% or more on 2 times the volume passes the test.

wrong.No; volume must be 5x the average: The test asks for 2 times the 50-day volume or more.
wrong.No; the gap down is under 4%: The open is more than 4% under the prior close, so it clears 4%.
wrong.Yes; the 2.4x volume alone is enough: Volume alone does not pass. The test also needs an open 4% or more under the prior close.

questions.story: A stock closed at 50.00. It opens at 47.80 and trades 2.4 times its 50-day average volume that day.
questions.simple: Yes. The open is more than 4% under the 50.00 close, and volume is more than twice the 50-day average.

reasons: the gap-and-volume stand-in is a proposed card line
the key rests on arithmetic from the story

questions.q: News Failure or plain Red to Green?
choices: Plain Red to Green; no news gap
News Failure; it reclaimed the close
Neither; it never closed green
News Failure; any gap down counts
questions.answer: Plain Red to Green; no news gap
questions.why: Plain Red to Green. The trigger is the same: price trades back over the prior close. The News Failure is that trigger on a 4% news gap with a named catalyst and twice the volume. A 1% gap on normal volume with no headline has none of the three.
questions.lesson_line: Same trigger, but the news and the gap make the News Failure.

wrong.News Failure; it reclaimed the close: A News Failure needs a big news gap, 4%, with a named catalyst and twice the volume.
wrong.Neither; it never closed green: The Red to Green trigger is price trading back over the prior close, and the story says it did.
wrong.News Failure; any gap down counts: Not any gap. It takes a 4% news gap with a named catalyst and twice the volume. This was 1% with no headline.

questions.story: A stock gaps down 1% on normal volume with no headline, then reclaims the prior close.
questions.simple: A plain Red to Green, because a News Failure also needs a 4% gap, twice the volume and real news.

deeper.trap: The trigger is the same, so the bar alone can fool you. What makes a News Failure is a named catalyst, a 4% news gap and twice the volume. Without them it is a plain Red to Green.

reasons: the 4% news gap is a proposed card line

questions.q: News Gapper or News Failure?
choices: News Gapper; the headline was good
News Failure; it closed red
Bear gap; the stock fell
questions.answer: News Failure; it closed red
questions.why: News Failure. Good news gapped it up and it closed red, under the prior close. A News Gapper holds the gap.
questions.lesson_line: Read the close against the prior close. Same headline, opposite trade.

wrong.News Gapper; the headline was good: A News Gapper closes green and holds the gap. This one closed red.
wrong.Bear gap; the stock fell: A bear gap starts with bad news. This was good news.

questions.story: A contract headline gaps a stock up 8%, and it closes 2% under the prior close.

questions.q: News Failure or earnings breakdown?
choices: News Failure; the headline was bad
News Gapper; the gap was big
Earnings breakdown; the news worked
questions.answer: Earnings breakdown; the news worked
questions.why: Earnings breakdown. Bad news gapped it down and it stayed down, so the news worked.
questions.lesson_line: If the gap keeps going, the news worked. Don't call it a failure.

wrong.News Failure; the headline was bad: A News Failure long closes back over the prior close. This one stayed down.
wrong.News Gapper; the gap was big: A News Gapper is a good-news gap that holds.

questions.story: An earnings miss gaps a stock down 9%. It closes at the low of the day, near the open.

questions.q: News Failure or Oops Reversal?
choices: Oops Reversal; there is no catalyst
News Failure; it reclaimed the close
News Failure; it opened under the low
Neither; an Oops needs news too
questions.answer: Oops Reversal; there is no catalyst
questions.why: Oops Reversal. An Oops needs an open under the prior low and a reclaim of the prior close on any day, news or not. A News Failure needs a dated catalyst behind the gap. With no news anywhere, it cannot be a News Failure.
questions.lesson_line: No catalyst, no News Failure. That is an Oops.

wrong.News Failure; it reclaimed the close: A News Failure needs a dated catalyst behind the gap. Here there is no news.
wrong.News Failure; it opened under the low: Opening under the prior low is the Oops part. A News Failure needs a dated catalyst behind the gap.
wrong.Neither; an Oops needs news too: An Oops needs no news. It needs an open under the prior low and a reclaim of the prior close.

questions.story: A stock opens under the prior low and reclaims the prior close. There is no news anywhere.
questions.simple: An Oops Reversal, because it opened under the prior low and came back with no news behind it.

reasons: what counts as news is a held decision (D-032)

questions.q: What does that tell you about the news?
choices: Twelve strong signals; short them all
The news was the market, not one stock
Each one is a separate catalyst
questions.answer: The news was the market, not one stock
questions.why: The news was the market, not the stock. Fewer than 5 such events on the same day is the line.
questions.lesson_line: A cluster of the same shape means a market story.

wrong.Twelve strong signals; short them all: A cluster means the news was the market, not the stock.
wrong.Each one is a separate catalyst: A same-day cluster is one market story.

questions.story: Twelve stocks show the bearish News Failure shape on the same day.

questions.q: What does that close tell you?
choices: Nothing; one close proves nothing
The trade is working; add more
The failure itself failed
questions.answer: The failure itself failed
questions.why: The failure itself failed. The next session closed back on the news side of the prior close.
questions.lesson_line: A close back on the news side means the failure failed.

wrong.Nothing; one close proves nothing: It is an invalidation. The failure itself failed.
wrong.The trade is working; add more: No adds. A close back on the news side says the idea failed.

questions.story: You bought the red-to-green on the news day. The next session closes under the pre-news close.

questions.q: Buy at market?
choices: No; over 4% past the trigger
Yes; it is still climbing
Yes, but only with half size
No; 2:30 is too late in the day
questions.answer: No; over 4% past the trigger
questions.why: No. 90.50 is more than 4% above the 86.35 prior close, the trigger. Never buy more than 4% above the buy point. Half size does not fix it, and the time of day is not the problem. Miss it and move on.
questions.lesson_line: Past 4% over the trigger, skip it. Miss it and move on.

wrong.Yes; it is still climbing: 90.50 is more than 4% above the 86.35 trigger. We skip it.
wrong.Yes, but only with half size: Half size does not fix a chase. Past 4% beyond the trigger, skip it.
wrong.No; 2:30 is too late in the day: We have no time-of-day rule. The problem is the price: more than 4% past the trigger.

questions.story: A News Failure long triggers at the 86.35 prior close. You check at 2:30, and it trades at 90.50.
questions.simple: No. At 90.50 the stock is more than 4% above the 86.35 close, so buying now is a chase and we skip it.

reasons: the key rests on arithmetic from the story
rests on the owner's rulebook (C28)

questions.q: Do you buy the red-to-green?
choices: Yes; the news is a different catalyst
No; a report is within 3 sessions
Yes; the reversal shows real strength
No; never buy on a gap-down day
questions.answer: No; a report is within 3 sessions
questions.why: No. No new buy or short in the 3 sessions before a scheduled report, and 2 sessions is inside that window. The conference headline is a different catalyst, but the report is still near. Buying on a gap-down day is fine on its own: the long is bought as price trades back over the prior close.
questions.lesson_line: A report within 3 sessions: wait.

wrong.Yes; the news is a different catalyst: A report within 3 sessions blocks a new buy, whatever the other news.
wrong.Yes; the reversal shows real strength: Strength does not move the earnings rule.
wrong.No; never buy on a gap-down day: The News Failure long is bought on the gap-down day, as price trades back over the prior close. The report is the problem.

questions.story: A stock gaps down on a conference headline and comes back over the prior close. Its earnings report is 2 sessions away.
questions.simple: No. The earnings report is only 2 sessions away, and we open no new trade in the 3 sessions before one.

reasons: rests on the owner's rulebook (B22)

questions.q: Is it a long?
choices: Yes; the shape is strong
Yes, with a tight stop
No; a long under the 200-day
questions.answer: No; a long under the 200-day
questions.why: No. The long needs a close above the 200-day, and 282.76 is under 288.05. No longs below the 200-day, unless parabolic.
questions.lesson_line: Right shape, wrong side of the 200-day. Pass.

wrong.Yes; the shape is strong: A strong shape under the 200-day is still the wrong side of the line.
wrong.Yes, with a tight stop: No longs below the 200-day, unless parabolic.

questions.story: A stock gaps down 5.2% on 2.1x volume and closes up 5.3% in the top 7% of the range. It closes at 282.76, under its 200-day at 288.05.

questions.q: Is it a short?
choices: No; shorts go under the 200-day
Yes; 2.7x volume is enough
Yes, if the stop is tight
No; it needs 3x 50-day volume
questions.answer: No; shorts go under the 200-day
questions.why: No. Shorts only below the 200-day, never above it unless it is a parabolic short. This close, 377.76, is above the 200-day at 358.04. The volume is enough: 2.7x clears the 2 times the test asks. The only gate that fails is the 200-day.
questions.lesson_line: Shorts live below the 200-day. This one is above.

wrong.Yes; 2.7x volume is enough: Shorts only below the 200-day, never above it unless parabolic.
wrong.Yes, if the stop is tight: A tight stop does not move the 200-day rule.
wrong.No; it needs 3x 50-day volume: The test asks for 2 times the 50-day volume, and 2.7x clears it. The 200-day is what fails.

questions.story: Good news gaps a stock up 5.0% on 2.7x volume. It closes down 0.2% in the bottom 18% of the range, at 377.76, above its 200-day at 358.04.
questions.simple: No. It closed above its 200-day line, and we only short stocks below that line unless the move is parabolic.

deeper.counter: A good-news gap that closes red near the low looks like a textbook short. Above the 200-day it is not ours unless it is a parabolic short. The shape can be perfect and the location still says no.

reasons: rests on the owner's rulebook (B26); the card's short location waits on D-009

questions.q: Which gate fails the News Failure?
choices: The fall; a 34% drop is too deep
The gap; it opened only 3.1% down
The volume; 2.5x is still too low
The close; 4.5% up is too small
questions.answer: The gap; it opened only 3.1% down
questions.why: The gap. The open was only 3.1% under the prior close. A News Failure needs a 4% news gap with a named catalyst and twice the volume. The earnings report is the catalyst, and 2.5x volume clears. Each near-miss fails exactly one gate, and here it is the gap. This one is a Red to Green day on an earnings report, not this setup.
questions.lesson_line: Check the gap size first. Under 4%, it is not a News Failure.

wrong.The volume; 2.5x is still too low: The test needs 2 times the volume, and 2.5x clears it.
wrong.The fall; a 34% drop is too deep: A deep fall is not a fail. The rule likes a stock that fell first, like one down 27% in 60 sessions.

questions.q: Hidden ticker, a news day after the close. It gapped down on heavy volume. Was there a valid red-to-green long that day?
choices: Not valid; the close stayed under it
Valid; it traded back over the close
Not valid; it gapped down, so it is weak
Valid; any gap down on volume counts
questions.answer: Valid; it traded back over the close
questions.why: Valid. It gapped down 5.5% on 2.1x volume, then traded back over the prior close, the red-to-green trigger. It closed 20.3% over that close, at 0.93 of its range. Our scan's buy was 86.36, a market order as it crossed. It reached 3R in 1 day. At the close it was far past the trigger, so the valid buy came earlier in the day.
questions.lesson_line: A gap that reverses to a strong close is the long.

wrong.Not valid; the close stayed under it: Look again: the close finished far over the prior close.
wrong.Not valid; it gapped down, so it is weak: A gap down that reverses is the setup, not a flaw.
wrong.Valid; any gap down on volume counts: A gap down alone is not the trigger. The long needs price back over the prior close. A gap that stays down means the news worked.

questions.simple: Yes, it was valid, because after the gap down the price climbed back over the prior close on the news day.

deeper.trap: The trap is judging it at the close. By then it was 20.3% over the prior close, far past the trigger. The card says to skip a stock already more than 4% past it. The valid buy was the red-to-green cross during the day, at 86.36 in our scan.

reasons: the red-to-green entry is proposed and the failure close is a held decision (D-087)

questions.q: Hidden ticker, a news day that gapped down and closed green. Take the long or pass?
choices: Take it; the reversal looks strong
Take it; the gap was large enough
Pass; it closed under the 200-day
Pass; it needs a close at the high
questions.answer: Pass; it closed under the 200-day
questions.why: Pass. It closed at 282.76, under the 200-day at 288.05. No longs below the 200-day simple moving average, unless it is a parabolic long. The reversal can look strong and the gap can be big enough. The 200-day still fails it: a reversal under the line is the wrong side of the average.
questions.lesson_line: A strong reversal under the 200-day is a pass.

wrong.Take it; the reversal looks strong: A strong reversal under the 200-day is the wrong side of the line.
wrong.Take it; the gap was large enough: A large gap does not lift the 200-day rule.
wrong.Pass; it needs a close at the high: A close in the top of the range grades a long up; it is not a gate. The 200-day is what fails.

questions.simple: Pass. The stock closed just under its 200-day line, and we take no longs below that line unless the move is parabolic.

deeper.trap: The close sits just under the 200-day, so the line is easy to miss if it is not on your chart. A strong green bar draws the eye first. Check the 200-day before you grade the reversal. Under it, a long is a pass however good the bar looks.

reasons: rests on the owner's rulebook (B26)
fixed before

questions.q: What does this market do for the long?
choices: It helps; it is where the long fits
It does not; longs want a hot market
It hurts; breadth should be strong
It only matters for the short side
questions.answer: It helps; it is where the long fits
questions.why: It helps. The card's long comes after a correction, near washed-out breadth. That is this market. A hot market is not the cue this long wants.
questions.lesson_line: A bad-news reversal in a washed-out market is a stronger read.

wrong.It does not; longs want a hot market: The long comes after a correction, near washed-out breadth.
wrong.It hurts; breadth should be strong: Washed-out breadth after a correction is where the long fits.
wrong.It only matters for the short side: The card gives the long a market cue too: after a correction, near washed-out breadth.

questions.story: The market just corrected hard, breadth is washed out, and the reading is turning back toward Green. A leader gaps down on bad news and recovers over the prior close.
questions.simple: A washed-out market after a correction helps the long, because that is where this reversal fits best.

deeper.counter: The same washed-out market cuts the other way for shorts. AMAT and DAL were shorted the day before a market rally, and both stops were hit the next day. Our research calls the bearish read in a washed-out market a poor sell signal.

reasons: rests on the criteria card's proposed criterion (owner default, not yet ruled) (nf.market_long)

questions.q: What is the right view?
choices: He is right; it is the bottom
One failure is a clue, not proof
Ignore it; it means nothing
It is a market sell signal
questions.answer: One failure is a clue, not proof
questions.why: One failure is a clue, not proof. Treating one failure as proof is a listed mistake. Shapiro himself wants two things: crowded positioning and market confirmation. One reversal in one name is a single clue. Weigh it with the market reading.
questions.lesson_line: A clue, not proof. Wait for the rest of the picture.

wrong.He is right; it is the bottom: Treating one failure as proof is a listed mistake.
wrong.Ignore it; it means nothing: It is a clue, not nothing. It adds to the picture without proving it.
wrong.It is a market sell signal: A bad-news gap that closes back green is the long side, not a sell. And one failure is still a clue, not proof.

questions.story: One bad-news reversal on a stock in your list closed green. A friend says that proves the market has bottomed.
questions.simple: One stock bouncing back on bad news is a clue, not proof that the market has bottomed.

deeper.trap: The trap runs both ways. One failure is not proof of a bottom, and one failure that loses is not proof the idea is dead. Our test found about two losses for every 3R winner, so a single case says little.

reasons: rests on the criteria card's listed mistake (house source)

questions.q: The stop for a News Failure short goes a few cents under the news day's low.
questions.answer: False
questions.why: False. For a short, the stop goes a few cents over the news day's high. For a long, it goes a few cents under the low. The stop sits beyond the news day's extreme so far, not exactly on it.
questions.lesson_line: Long: under the low. Short: over the high.
questions.simple: False, because a short's stop goes a few cents above the news day's high, not under its low.

reasons: rests on the owner's rulebook (section 9) (F62); the card's settled stop

questions.q: A News Failure long is bought at the open on the news day.
questions.answer: False
questions.why: False. The buy is a market order as price trades back over the prior close on the news day, not at the open.
questions.lesson_line: Wait for the trade back over the prior close.

questions.q: In our test, News Failure longs closing in the top quarter of the range reached 3R more often than all longs.
questions.answer: False
questions.why: False. In our test, longs that closed in the top quarter of the range reached 3R 31% of the time, across 500 events. All longs reached it 32.0% of the time. On the card, a top-quarter close after an undercut raises the grade. In our test, the top-quarter close did not make 3R more likely.
questions.lesson_line: A strong shape raises the grade. It never guarantees a win.
questions.simple: False, because in our test top-quarter longs reached 3R 31% of the time, against 32.0% for all longs.

deeper.example: Our scan of 1,534 events found 33.4% reached 3R and 17.9% reached 5R before the stop. The top-quarter longs did no better, 31% to 3R.

reasons: rests on the criteria card's proposed criterion (owner default, not yet ruled) (nf.grade_shape)

questions.q: Short at 15.26 with the stop at 16.05. How far over the entry is the stop, in percent?
questions.why: 5.2. That is past our usual 3%, so the size comes from the stop. SKIN's stop was exactly that wide.
questions.lesson_line: The short's stop sits over the entry. Measure it in percent too.

questions.q: Between which two R levels does the stop move to breakeven?
choices: Between 2R and 5R
Between 0.5R and 1R
Between 3R and 6R
Between 6R and 8R
questions.answer: Between 2R and 5R
questions.why: Between 2R and 5R. Our rule says to move the stop to breakeven at 2R to 5R, ideally. The card's default is the first trim, and the hard rule for that trim is a third at 3R. Breakeven means the stop sits at your entry price. It is a window, not a fixed point.
questions.lesson_line: Breakeven comes between 2R and 5R, at the first trim.

wrong.Between 0.5R and 1R: That is far too early. The window is 2R to 5R.
wrong.Between 6R and 8R: That is past the window. Breakeven comes between 2R and 5R.
wrong.Between 3R and 6R: That is the window for the first trim. Breakeven comes between 2R and 5R.

questions.simple: The stop moves up to your entry price somewhere between 2R and 5R, usually when you take the first trim.

reasons: rests on the owner's rulebook (section 9) (B19)

questions.q: Where does the stop go by default?
choices: Up to breakeven, at 31.83
Stays at 30.23 until it hits 5R
Up under the 10-day average
Up to 3R, where you just sold
questions.answer: Up to breakeven, at 31.83
questions.why: Up to breakeven, 31.83. The stop moves to breakeven between 2R and 5R, at the first trim by default. You just took the first third at 3R, so the stop goes to your entry. It only moves up, never down or wider. The 10-day trail comes later, for the last third.
questions.lesson_line: First trim off, stop up to your entry.

wrong.Stays at 30.23 until it hits 5R: Breakeven comes between 2R and 5R, at the first trim by default. Do not wait for 5R.
wrong.Up under the 10-day average: The 10-day is the trail for the last third. The stop moves to breakeven first.
wrong.Up to 3R, where you just sold: The stop goes to breakeven, your entry, at the first trim by default. Not up to the trim price.

questions.story: You bought a News Failure long at 31.83 with the stop at 30.23. The stock reaches 3R and you sell the first third.
questions.simple: The stop moves up to your 31.83 entry, because the first trim is when breakeven comes by default.

reasons: rests on the owner's rulebook (section 9) (B19, A4)

questions.q: Bought at 86.36 with the stop at 81.48. Where is 5R?
questions.why: 110.76. One R is the buy minus the stop: 86.36 minus 81.48. Add five of those to the buy. After the first third at 3R, another third comes off at 5R, then the last third rides the trail.
questions.lesson_line: Know your 5R before the open. The second third comes off there.
questions.simple: $110.76. One R is the buy minus the stop, and 5R adds five of those to the buy.

reasons: computed key
rests on the owner's rulebook (E51)

questions.q: The News Failure plan sells half the position at 5R.
questions.answer: False
questions.why: False. We sell, or cover, a third at 5R, not half. The plan is a third at 3R, a third at 5R, then trail the last third.
questions.lesson_line: A third at 3R, a third at 5R, the rest on the trail.
questions.simple: False, because the plan sells a third at 5R, not half, and the last third rides the trail.

deeper.counter: The hard rule is a third at 3R, then a third at 5R. Our rulebook also says the first trim is ideally anywhere from 3R to 6R. In practice, we mostly wait for 5R. The courses teach the hard rule.

reasons: rests on the owner's rulebook (section 9) (E51, B19)

questions.q: What do you do at the open?
choices: Take the first third off now
Wait for a dip back to the 3R level
Sell half now and half at 5R
Hold it all and move the stop up
questions.answer: Take the first third off now
questions.why: Take the first third off now, at the open. If a stock opens past a trim level, take that trim at the open. The open at 38.10 is past your 3R level, so the first third comes off there. Do not wait for a dip back. After the trim, the stop can move up to breakeven.
questions.lesson_line: Gap past a trim level: take it at the open.

wrong.Sell half now and half at 5R: The plan is a third at 3R and another third at 5R, not halves.
wrong.Hold it all and move the stop up: The stop can follow after the trim. The trim itself comes off at the open.
wrong.Wait for a dip back to the 3R level: A dip may never come. A trim level the day opens past is taken at the open.

questions.story: You bought a News Failure long at 31.83 with the stop at 30.23. Next morning it opens at 38.10, above your 3R level, and you have sold nothing.
questions.simple: Take the first third off right at the open, because the price opened above your 3R level and that trim is due.

reasons: rests on the owner's rulebook (section 9) (F63, B19)

questions.q: A News Failure short that gaps down past a trim level covers that trim at the open.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. If it opens past a trim level, take that trim at the open. For a short, past means lower, so a gap down through 3R or 5R covers that third at the open.
questions.lesson_line: Gap past a trim level: take the trim at the open, long or short.
questions.simple: True, because a gap past a trim level is taken at the open, and for a short, past means lower.

reasons: rests on the owner's rulebook (section 9) (F63); short side is a mirror

questions.q: Your News Failure short also qualifies as a parabolic short. Where is the cover target?
choices: At the daily 9 EMA
At the daily 21 EMA
At the 50-day SMA
At the 200-day SMA
questions.answer: At the daily 9 EMA
questions.why: At the daily 9 EMA. If the short also qualifies as a parabolic short, it uses Bracco's 9 EMA target instead of the trims. Our rule says the same: a parabolic short's target is the 9-day average. The 21-day is a trail for steadier movers, not this target.
questions.lesson_line: A parabolic short covers at the 9 EMA, not on the trims.

wrong.At the daily 21 EMA: The 21-day is a trail for a steadier mover. Bracco's parabolic target is the 9 EMA.
wrong.At the 50-day SMA: The 50-day is not the target. Bracco's target for a parabolic short is the 9 EMA.
wrong.At the 200-day SMA: The 200-day is the line for the side rule, not the cover target.

questions.simple: Cover at the daily 9 EMA, because a parabolic short uses that average as its target instead of the usual trims.

deeper.trap: The trap is mixing the two plans. A plain News Failure short covers a third at 3R and a third at 5R, then trails the rest. Once it qualifies as a parabolic short, the 9 EMA target replaces those trims.

reasons: rests on the owner's rulebook (section 9) (D47); the card's settled parabolic target

questions.q: In our rulebook, what makes a move parabolic?
choices: A 3-5 day burst, a final leg
One big gap on twice the volume
A slow climb over many months
A close far above the 200-day
questions.answer: A 3-5 day burst, a final leg
questions.why: A 3-5 day burst. Our rulebook defines parabolic as a 3-5 day final leg. Its boxes include three straight up days and a gap up on the climax day. The more boxes checked, the stronger. For a long it is the mirror image, a burst down.
questions.simple: A short, fast burst: a 3-5 day final leg, such as three straight up days. For a long, it is a burst down.
questions.lesson_line: Parabolic means a 3-5 day burst, the final leg. The more boxes checked, the stronger.

wrong.One big gap on twice the volume: That is the news stand-in, one day. Parabolic is a 3-5 day final leg.
wrong.A slow climb over many months: Parabolic is fast: a 3-5 day final leg, with three straight up days.
wrong.A close far above the 200-day: Parabolic is counted in boxes over a 3-5 day final leg, like two straight overnight gap ups.

reasons: rests on the owner's rulebook (B26)
